1	We have entered the
2	final stretch
3	of the end of the current year,
4	toward the coming year, which will be good for us.
5	Yesterday was Chai Elul,
6	the birthday of the Baal Shem Tov and the Alter Rebbe,
7	the Admor HaZaken.
8	We begin, as the Rebbe says, a run of twelve days
9	until the eve of Rosh Hashanah that is coming to us for good, including, of course,
10	that these twelve days correspond, one day to each month.
11	That is, each one of these days has the power
12	both to complete and repair what was lacking in the service of
13	HaShem in that month during the past year,
14	and to give us strength for the proper and fitting preparation
15	for that same month in the coming year,
16	for good.
17	And
18	as much as
19	we have spoken several times and emphasized
20	how precious the time of the month of Elul is, that on every
21	day and every moment of Elul the King, the King of kings of
22	kings, the Holy One, Blessed be He, is in the field,
23	and anyone who simply wants to has the ability and
24	the opportunity to approach Him
25	and ask of Him what he wants, and He receives
26	everyone with a pleasant countenance and a shining face,
27	everyone. Everyone. That is, He is in an
28	uplifted mood, and He only waits and hopes that a Jew will turn
29	to Him, that a Jew will connect with Him.
30	So it is clear that the whole time of the month of Elul is a
31	most precious time.
32	All the more so, within Elul itself,
33	we go up a level, or as we said before, we arrive at
34	the final stretch, the last twelve days, in which,
35	in such a condensed and concentrated way,
36	a Jew has the power to repair a whole month
37	in a single day. Do the simple math: every day
38	we have 24 hours in a day and we have 30
39	days in a month.
40	That means one can repair a whole day in less than an hour,
41	if we want to compare it in terms of time. But
42	this only illustrates
43	the greatness of these days. And therefore,
44	how much a Jew must pay attention to every detail
45	in thought, in speech, in action,
46	and in the matters he is engaged in. And above all
47	to the inner teshuvah that awakens within him.
48	With all five letters of Elul, the acronyms we already spoke
49	about in the past, which correspond to the whole of a Jew's
50	service of HaShem: his Torah study,
51	his prayer service, giving tzedakah and acts of
52	kindness, which also includes embellishing all the mitzvot,
53	all of them. And to do all this in the manner of teshuvah,
54	in a way that I truly want to return, to come back to
55	HaShem, to be face to face with HaShem, may He be blessed,
56	even if, Heaven forbid, I feel that I turned my back on Him
57	during the year and forgot the connection and did not behave
58	properly. Then I know that at every moment, and especially
59	in this month, I have the ability to do teshuvah, to make
60	one movement
61	that turns a state of turning the back into a state of face to face,
62	turning my face to HaShem.
63	And the
64	main point that the Rebbe renews for us in our generation is that all
65	of a Jew's service must be in the manner of
66	redemption, in such a way that he does not only think about his
67	personal connection with HaShem and his own spiritual good,
68	but thinks about the entire world.
69	He makes the soul-searching of the whole world: that the
70	time of the redemption has already come, and there is no explanation and no reason
71	in the world to delay the redemption even one moment.
72	And therefore he constantly has an inner cry to the Holy
73	One, Blessed be He: how long until He brings the redemption already?
74	And also a feeling of full personal responsibility to do
75	everything in his power to hasten the redemption.
76	So in order to understand the depth behind the
77	precious and special time we are in,
78	everything, after all, is by Divine Providence and directed from above.
79	So the order is that this Shabbat we read Parashat Ki
80	Tavo: "And it shall be, when you come into the land."
81	This Parashah opens
82	with a very, very special
83	mitzvah,
84	the mitzvah of the first fruits, Bikurim.
85	And after the Torah speaks in detail about this mitzvah,
86	which we will speak about a bit more shortly, there is
87	a sharp turn.
88	After
89	from the beginning of Devarim, "These are the words that Moshe
90	spoke to the children of Israel in the plains of Moab," Moshe
91	Rabbeinu, in the last month, the last month and a bit
92	of his life, his birthday and passing being on the seventh of Adar,
93	the people of Israel entered the Land in the month of Nissan, forty
94	years after they left Egypt.
95	A month before that was the passing of Moshe Rabbeinu,
96	on the seventh of Adar. So who brought them into the Land? Yehoshua,
97	of course.
98	But Moshe Rabbeinu himself, from Rosh Chodesh Shevat, which is
99	37 days before the seventh of Adar, began to explain to the people of
100	Israel all the words of the Torah
101	and to review all the mitzvot.
102	And
103	the purpose was, in essence, that after
104	the course of forty years in the desert, which began with the giving of the Torah,
105	at which a covenant was made between the people of Israel and the Holy One,
106	Blessed be He, once again, in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho,
107	another covenant is made between the people of Israel and the Holy One,
108	Blessed be He.
109	So if so,
110	what is the order? The order is that until
111	the end of the previous Parashah, Ki Teitzei, the individual
112	mitzvot are mentioned. And this is very prominent precisely
113	in that last Parashah, which is in fact the Parashah with
114	the most mitzvot, since every verse is yet another
115	mitzvah.
116	But after Moshe Rabbeinu finishes explaining all
117	the individual mitzvot,
118	he begins to speak about the general covenant between us
119	and HaShem, may He be blessed,
